subject: Under-stairs storage designed to fit
hook: A sale shoe rack fills the front of the cupboard. A pull-out uses all of it.
ig:
A sale shoe rack fills the front of the cupboard. A pull-out uses all of it.

It is Black Friday, and plenty of storage will be bought today that sits in the first half-metre of an under-stairs cupboard while the back fills with things nobody can reach.

The detail that fixes it is simple: a tall pull-out that runs the full depth of the space.

Why it works:
- Everything is reachable from the hallway, front to back.
- Each pull-out can be set up for one job: coats, shoes, cleaning kit.
- The units step down with the stairs, so even the low end earns its keep.
- Soft-close runners mean they glide shut rather than bang.

The trade-off is that each pull-out needs clear space in front of it to open, so it suits hallways with room to stand. Where the hall is tight, a hinged door with internal shelving can work better.

Which would suit your hallway? Tell us in the comments, and see our made-to-measure range via the link in bio.
fb:
Black Friday is full of storage boxes and shoe racks. They are handy, but under the stairs they usually end up stacked at the front while the back becomes a black hole.

The detail we would point you to instead is a full-depth pull-out. It slides right out into the hallway, so the coat or bag at the very back is as easy to grab as the one at the front. Stepped to the slope of the stairs, a run of them uses the whole space.

One thing to bear in mind: they need room in front to open, so very narrow halls can suit hinged doors better.
